Very disappointing customer service

Unfortunately, this wasn’t my first experience with poor customer service at this Baby Bunting store.

Today, I visited with my newborn specifically to try on an Ergobaby carrier. There were two staff members assisting one customer, while I was standing nearby waiting to be acknowledged. I asked where the Ergobaby carriers were and whether I could try one on. One staff member simply gestured for me to wait.

After waiting for a while, I asked if someone was going to assist me. A staff member eventually came over, but I then heard them make a comment to the other staff member implying that I was being rude. The other customer was also looking at me strangely, which made the whole situation very uncomfortable.

I explained to the staff member that I wasn’t trying to be rude. I was simply asking for assistance because there were two staff members with one customer while I was standing there with my newborn. I understand the other customer was asking questions, but a simple “We’ll be with you shortly” would have been enough.

What makes this more frustrating is that I’ve experienced something similar at this store before. On a previous visit, there were around three staff members talking together while I was clearly a customer standing there awkwardly wondering who was going to assist me. Again, nobody acknowledged me.

There was also an issue with the advice I was given about the Ergobaby carrier. The staff member told me that because my baby is still a newborn, her legs should be tucked inside the carrier. I later checked the manufacturer’s guidance for the Ergobaby Embrace and found that this advice was incorrect. As a new parent, I find this particularly concerning because I was specifically relying on the staff for guidance on using a newborn carrier safely.

I don’t expect staff to drop everything the moment another customer walks in, but I do expect to be acknowledged, treated respectfully and given accurate information—especially when I’m shopping for products for my newborn.

Very poor customer service and a really disappointing experience

one_star_reviews.text:
The pool itself is good and I have no complaint with the product. My issue is with the communication throughout, how the surrounding trades were handled, and how the company responded when there was a problem.

Communication was a constant frustration. I was regularly given dates or told someone would attend, and then no one would show or update me, which left me chasing and rearranging my own time around visits that did not happen. I was originally told the build would take 8 weeks. The contract stated 12. It ended up taking 19 weeks, and there was still work outstanding at the end that they held no responsibility for.

Leisure also organised and booked a tradesman for part of my job. They coordinated the work, gave the tradesman my details, and provided them with the plans. I was simply told I would be paying him. When that work was not done to standard, I was told the company had only "provided a name" and that everything else was my responsibility. That is not what happened. They booked and coordinated the trade, and I only received the tradesman's details after all of that had already been arranged.

When I raised this and pointed out what had actually taken place, the response did not change. I was told it was not their responsibility. They did offer to fix the issue, but only at a high fee, with no willingness to meet in the middle. When you spend $70,000 on a pool, you expect a problem like this to be resolved smoothly and reasonably, not met with a flat "not our problem."

My advice to anyone considering Leisure is to get every inclusion and every trade responsibility clearly in writing before you sign, and to confirm exactly who is accountable for what. Do not assume anything is covered unless it is written into the contract. The build may be fine, but be prepared for poor communication and to be on your own if something needs sorting out afterward.

one_star_reviews.text:
I expected much better from R.M.Williams Sunshine Plaza.

I went into this store specifically to purchase a Drover Belt. I tried on a size 36, it fitted correctly, and that was the size I decided to buy.

The sales assistant then went out the back to get me a new belt in a box. I had absolutely no reason to think I needed to check the size because I had just tried on a 36 and naturally assumed she was bringing me a new size 36.

She gave me a size 38.

Initially I could wear it on the tightest hole, but after wearing it for a while and the leather settling and stretching, it became too large.

I returned to the Sunshine Plaza store and explained exactly what had happened. I wasn't asking to return something because I'd changed my mind or because I'd selected the wrong size. Their staff member had simply given me a different size from the one I'd tried on and asked to purchase.

The solution offered by the store was basically to buy another belt. To make matters worse, the price had increased by around $20 by then.

So I was expected to pay again, at a higher price, to correct a mistake made by the store.

I subsequently contacted R.M.Williams customer service on 14 June. They finally responded on 4 September after admitting my enquiry had been "inadvertently missed". They then refused an exchange, partly because my receipt says size 38.

Of course it says size 38. That's the wrong size the salesperson handed me. That's the entire reason for the complaint.

They also referred to the amount of time that had passed, despite taking nearly three months themselves to respond to my complaint.

I like R.M.Williams products and have always regarded the brand as representing quality. Unfortunately, my experience at the Sunshine Plaza store didn't come close to the standard I'd expect when paying premium prices.

Mistakes happen. Handing me a 38 instead of a 36 is an understandable human error. What isn't acceptable is refusing to take responsibility for it when I returned to the store and expecting me to spend more money to fix their mistake.

Perhaps losing one customer doesn't mean much to a company the size of R.M.Williams. But this experience has certainly changed the way I view the brand and, particularly, this store.
